nodes.label: Reader memory strategy (SPEC §9)
nodes.rationale: The Xiaomi MiBox 4 (2 GB) is the performance floor: decode only a small window, virtualize vertical lists, decode at screen size, limit concurrency, and fix the image cap measured in Fase 0.

nodes.label: Module installation threat model (SPEC §7.2)
nodes.rationale: Malicious repos are countered by user-added repos plus confirmation; tampered packages by HTTPS+SHA-256; hostile scripts have no real isolation in v1 (D-5), trust rests on the repo; deep links never auto-install.

nodes.label: Design source authority order (SPEC §11.1)
nodes.rationale: Prevents agents copying exported Stitch HTML/Tailwind: SPEC wins on functionality, DESIGN_RULES on content/color, DESIGN.md on appearance, PNG over HTML on composition, and doubts are asked, never silently decided.

nodes.label: Definition of Done
nodes.rationale: Common quality bar per task: all acceptance criteria met, lint/typecheck/test/build green, tests that would fail if functionality removed, MEMORY.md entry, one commit per task.

nodes.label: ADR-0001 stack and conventions
nodes.rationale: Records (not reopens) the adopted stack: SPEC D-1..D-13, MEMORY.md P-1..P-12, and plan tech choices (pnpm, Vitest, fflate, @noble/hashes, htmlparser2+css-select, better-sqlite3); resolves P-n ID collisions by fixing MEMORY.md as canonical.

nodes.label: ADR-0002 versions and memory budget
nodes.rationale: Fixes Expo SDK ~57.0.28 / RN 0.86.3 / React 19.2.3 / TS ~6.0.3; confirms minSdk 28 (Android 9) works on the MiBox 4; pure-JS libs (@noble/hashes, fflate, htmlparser2) smoke-tested 3/3 OK on phones; cold-start and memory numbers per device; image memory cap measured via the apps/mobile calibration panel.

nodes.label: RyuuNest SPEC (authoritative specification)
nodes.rationale: Ordered authority: SPEC decides what the app does; DESIGN_RULES/DESIGN.md decide looks; PNG composition; HTML reference only; IDEA.md is context.

nodes.label: Expo Router navigation convention (apps/mobile)
nodes.rationale: All navigation in the Expo app uses Expo Router with routes in src/app/; non-route code stays outside to keep the file-based router clean.

nodes.label: Dragon 'guarida' visual identity concept
nodes.rationale: The app should feel like a personal digital lair (biblioteca fantástica + otaku aesthetic + dragon mascot); fantasy belongs to exploration and disappears in the reader.

nodes.label: 'El lector es sagrado' design principle
nodes.rationale: The app looks special while exploring and disappears while reading: ambient theming and the dragon never overlay reading content.

nodes.label: RyuuNest project vision (IDEA)
nodes.rationale: Existing reader apps break when sites change or are abandoned; RyuuNest is a maintainable personal core (reader, favorites, progress, module manager) where fixing a site means updating a module, running on-device with no backend, GPL-3.0.

nodes.label: Architecture decisions D-1..D-13
nodes.rationale: Pure-TS monorepo core, React Native (Expo) with TV variant, separate web client, two-level modules (declarative/script), zip packages with hash, SQLite/IndexedDB, no server/accounts, Android 9 minimum for MiBox 4, JSON backup in v1, GPL-3.0, one folder per favorite, four media kinds including manhwa.

nodes.label: Plan technical decisions P-1..P-14
nodes.rationale: pnpm+Vitest, fflate for zip, @noble/hashes for SHA-256 (RN lacks Web Crypto), htmlparser2+css-select (no Node APIs), abstract Storage with thin SqlDriver, better-sqlite3 for CI, real-site modules live outside the repo, test-site as reusable package, module limits kept at SPEC §7.1, bd local tracker now and GitHub Issues later; local P-n IDs must not be cited (P-35).

nodes.label: Vertical cut build strategy
nodes.rationale: Instead of building all layers, each phase delivers a complete verifiable path (install module, declarative module, script module, library, progress, backup) with tests as the tip.

nodes.label: Web to extension HTTP bridge protocol (SPEC §10)
nodes.norm_label: web to extension http bridge protocol (spec §10)
nodes.rationale: Web runs modules in a DOM-less Web Worker; all network goes through the browser extension, which only answers the app origin and user-authorized domains.

nodes.label: Script module template (module-sdk)
nodes.rationale: Script module exports create(host) and may only use host.*; the host enforces domain permissions, timeout, concurrency cap and pacing.

nodes.label: Host network layer (host.fetch)
nodes.rationale: Modules never make requests themselves; they ask the host (host.fetch), which applies headers, cookies and permissions.
